claims.text: Existing text summarization methods suffer from hallucinations where generated summaries contain information not present in the source text.
Existing hallucination detection and mitigation methods lack transparency in their underlying mechanisms.
The proposed Question-Answer Generation, Sorting, and Evaluation (Q-S-E) methodology enables quantitative detection of hallucinations in summaries.
The proposed iterative hallucination resolution mechanism enhances the transparency of the modification process.
The proposed framework significantly improves the factual consistency of summaries across CNN/Daily Mail, PubMed, and ArXiv datasets.
The proposed framework preserves the informational completeness of summaries while improving factual consistency.
